takeaways: Every interactive element shows a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus.
Design it. Do not leave it to the browser default, and never remove it.
A good target, from 2.4.13: a 2px outline, offset from the element, with 3:1 contrast.
It has to work on every background the component sits on.
failures: The outline removed in the stylesheet
A focus style so faint nobody notices it
Custom components with no focus state drawn
check: Tab through the prototype or build. Can you always tell where you are?
Check the focus style on light, dark and image backgrounds.
Include a focus state in every component’s state list.

quiz.question: A designer removes the focus outline because mouse users see it after clicking. What is the best response?
options: Keep a designed style that shows for keyboard focus
Replace it with a color change on hover
quiz.why: Developers can show the ring only for keyboard use. Hover does nothing for people who do not use a pointer.

spec: Draw the focus state for every interactive component.
Give the ring’s width, offset and color as values.
Show it on each surface color the component can sit on.
review: Where is the focus state for this component?
Does the ring survive on the darkest and lightest backgrounds?
Does a sticky bar ever cover the focused element? That is 2.4.11.
tradeoff: A strong ring can clash with a refined style. A two-tone ring, light and dark together, stays visible everywhere and can be tuned to the brand.
system: One focus token, applied by every component. Nobody should design a focus ring twice.
pitch: Without visible focus, a keyboard user is operating your product blindfolded.
